bottlenecks.reading: What TSLA supplies that is scarce: deployable firm power and grid-compliance capacity, from stock, for utilities and data centers, through Megapack. Tesla's own Q3 2026 update says storage demand is its 'highest-ever order rate and backlog' (no figure given), calls storage 'the fastest way to add power to the existing grid' and ties it to data-center uptime, while Q3 deployments were 13.7 GWh (+9.6% on Q3 2025's 12.5) and Q3 energy revenue fell 15.6% to 2,881 usd mn (tariff-related customer refunds named by management). The market is growing: US installations hit a record 18.9 GWh in Q2 2026 (Wood Mackenzie / American Clean Power); competitor Fluence reports a record 6.4 usd bn backlog (+30% on a year earlier), 1.44 usd bn of orders in its June quarter, and 850 usd mn of data-center awards through July. Who adds capacity: Tesla lists 110 GWh of installed Megapack capacity (California 40, Shanghai 20, Texas 50; Texas began production in Q3) against a Q3 deployment pace of about 55 GWh a year; Fluence is adding contract manufacturing but delays cut its fiscal 2026 revenue guide by 0.4 usd bn at the midpoint. So integration capacity is being added faster than deployments; the binding constraints are cells and delivery execution, and how long the shortage lasts is not in the sources (the data-center link is management's reading).

Battery cells (and the lithium behind them) are the scarce input for both vehicles and storage. Tesla's 10-K says it relies on suppliers such as Panasonic and CATL for cells and has so far fully qualified only a very limited number of suppliers; in response it is building its own supply: 4680 cells above 40 GWh in Texas (production), LFP cells 7 GWh in Nevada (early ramp), lithium refining 30 GWh of cathode-equivalent capacity in Texas (early ramp; the in-house lithium refinery began operating in January 2026) and the first Megapacks with U.S.-built LFP cells shipped in Q3 2026. Competitors show the same bottleneck: BYD's first-half 2026 sales were hit by second-generation Blade battery shortages (press), and Fluence booked about 15 usd mn of upfront cost for a long-term international battery supply agreement. The duration of the constraint and the in-house ramp rates are not quantified in the sources.

In vehicles TSLA does not supply a scarce thing today: demand and price are the constraint, not capacity. Q3 2026 deliveries were 486,532 against 497,099 a year earlier (-2%), with global days of supply at 11 and installed vehicle capacity far above deliveries; global plug-in and electric sales were 2.15 million in September 2026 (-2% on a year earlier) and 15.5 million year to date (+3%), with Europe +30%, North America -24% and China -13% year to date (Benchmark Mineral Intelligence via The EV Report). Management still describes demand as strong in several markets; the sources show a market that is flat in units and moving to Europe and exports, where BYD is adding volume.

The scarce thing in autonomy is licensed, safety-validated unsupervised driving at scale. Waymo, the benchmark, reports about 500,000 paid rides a week earlier in 2026, roughly 3,500 robotaxis, over 20 million trips and driverless service in 11 cities (press relay of Waymo statements). Tesla's own Q3 update reports nearly 2 million cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles by quarter-end, Austin hours 6 am to midnight, first Cybercab units added to the Austin fleet, and FSD (Supervised) approved in nine EU countries with over 100,000 customers there; the 10-K warns that EU and national rules 'may hinder or complicate' autonomous vehicles and a ride-hailing business. Paid adoption in Tesla's own numbers so far is FSD subscriptions lifting automotive ancillary sales and a record Services and Other gross profit of 734 usd mn (a wider line than FSD). Units differ (Tesla miles, Waymo trips), so the scale gap is directional, not a ratio.

Hypothesis only: humanoid robots (Optimus) as a scarce, high-value product. The Q3 2026 update says production of Optimus began on the Fremont high-volume lines ('early ramp') with a Texas plant under construction; the documents read give no paid customers, price or revenue, so there is no paid adoption to underwrite.

dc FRESHNESS: the latest results are Q3 2026 (deck and 8-K 2026-10-21, 10-Q 2026-10-22). Reported to the 10-Q date: revenue 28,046M flat year over year, gross profit 5,494M (19.6% margin), operating income 718M (2.6%), net income to common 787M, EPS 0.22 diluted (non-GAAP 0.48), operating cash flow 6,263M, capex 4,732M, free cash flow 1,531M, cash and short-term investments 45,447M.

dc MGMT 2026-10-21 (CFO Taneja, call): FY2026 capex guidance revised to 'approximately $20 billion' (from 'in excess of $25 billion' in the 10-Qs of 2026-04-23 and 2026-07-23) 'as a result of managing our capital deployment efficiently', funded primarily from operating cash flow. The 10-Q of 2026-10-22 says 'in excess of $20 billion'. Nine-month capex is 13,014M, so the guide implies about 7.0bn in Q4 2026. Capex 'for the next few years would continue to expand' (Robotaxi fleet, Optimus capacity, solar, self-driving compute, a semiconductor fab); Musk: capex 'a little lower than we anticipated', 'more meaningful next year and then noticeable, in the tens of billions, in 2028'. This is management's statement, not a forecast of this engine.

dc MGMT 2026-10-21 (CFO, 10-Q Liquidity): in September 2026 Tesla signed three unsecured credit agreements with aggregate commitments of $30 billion (a $20bn delayed-draw term loan maturing 2029-09 whose undrawn commitment steps down to $10bn at 12 months, $5bn at 15 months and zero at 18 months; $8bn 5-year and $2bn 364-day revolvers replacing the $5bn RCF). 'We don't plan to make any draws under any of the new facilities in this calendar year.' The 10-Q also says heightened capex 'will necessitate additional funding beyond our operating cash flow' and that the business 'may include additional funding': external funding is a stated possibility, not a plan with an amount.

dc MGMT 2026-10-21 (CFO, call): operating expenses 'as previously guided' keep rising sequentially (R&D 2,761M versus 2,371M in Q2 and 1,630M a year ago: SI and self-driving costs including compute depreciation, chip development, preproduction costs for Optimus, Megapack 3 and Semi; SBC from the 2025 CEO award); 'This trend of growing OpEx would continue until we commercialize these new products.' No numeric opex guide.

dc MGMT 2026-10-21 (Musk and CFO, call): demand 'is exceeding our production by a significant margin'; the highest passenger-vehicle backlog in four years; deliveries constrained primarily by production, and the deck names battery availability as the limiting factor on the vehicle production ramp; days of supply 11. FSD is 'the biggest driver for demand'; over 75% of North American deliveries signed up for a paid FSD subscription at delivery (each delivery carries a free month); 1.74M active FSD subscriptions. Musk expects EU-wide FSD approval 'maybe within a few months... surprised if it takes longer than Q1' (2027); nine EU countries approved so far. Opinion and management expectation, not evidence of outcome.

dc MGMT 2026-10-21 (CFO, call): automotive gross margin excluding regulatory credits rose from 16.3% to 18.1% sequentially, 'driven by a higher mix of deliveries in APAC'; commodity price increases and interest rate changes are headwinds partly offset by changes to the vehicle financing programs; Model S and X were discontinued in mid-2026 (10-Q). Energy gross margin rose from 20.4% to 33.1%, 'primarily attributed to tariff refunds recognized in the quarter and warranty true-downs resulting from alignment with our vendor on certain cell-related costs to be reimbursed by them' (the warranty amount is not given); Taneja expects ASP improvement and further margin improvement as Megapack production rises. Services and other margin 15.9%, an all-time high. Management says Megapack is 'almost sold out' for 2027, with the highest-ever order rate and backlog, driven by data center demand.

dc MGMT 2026-10-21 (call): Robotaxi: Cybercab rides began in Austin on 2026-09-03; the Cybercab fleet in Austin grew tenfold in a month; Dallas next month; six cities in the Robotaxi service; 24/7 operation and higher-speed roads targeted by year end; a $0.30 per paid mile unit-economics goal (whether it is a cost or a price per mile is not stated) is not yet reached, with a 'path' to it; customer-owned vehicles joining the fleet around Q2 2027 (v15 software); Cybercab to customers 'by the end of this year' in small numbers (the vast majority of the fleet will be Tesla-owned). Musk: Robotaxi 'will not move the needle this quarter', 'noticeable probably in Q2' 2027 and 'a big deal by Q3 or Q4 of next year'. These are management hypotheses without revenue disclosure.

dc MGMT 2026-10-21 (call): Optimus: early production on the Fremont line (a 1-million-unit-per-line design) 'at least a year, maybe a little longer' to reach an annualized rate of 20,000 units a week; design still changing (the hand); deliveries to outside companies 'toward the end of next year' (2027); AI5 chip integration around April 2027; 10,000-20,000 bots needed for self-play data; an Austin Optimus factory is under construction. Terafab: the Austin research fab begins commissioning machinery in H1 2027, a first test chip around May or June 2027, useful chips at volume 'around Q3 of 2028' (aspirational); capital 'in the tens of billions' up to early 2028 and 'north of $100 billion' long term, with the Tesla versus SpaceX split not yet decided. Vehicle capacity: 'aiming for 5 million vehicles a year by approximately 2030' (Musk: 'a good shot'); Berlin expansion permits applied for; Semi factory in Nevada started. All are management aspirations.

market_direction.reading: Vehicles: flat in units and shifting by region. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence (relayed by The EV Report) counts 15.5 million plug-in and electric sales in January-September 2026 (+3% on a year earlier; plug-in hybrids included) and 2.15 million in September (-2%), with Europe +30%, North America -24% and China -13% year to date. Tesla's own revenue follows the same map: Q3 2026 United States -14.4% and China -7.9% while Other international +31.8%; the nine-month total +12.5% came entirely from Other international (+49.1%) (my arithmetic on the 10-Q regional facts). US policy is moving away from EV support: Tesla's regulatory-credit revenue fell from 417M (Q3 2025) to 113M (Q3 2026, after a 475M contractual reversal) and that program's remaining performance obligations from 841M to 384M. Storage: growing and pulled by data centers: record US installations of 18.9 GWh in Q2 2026 (Wood Mackenzie / American Clean Power, US only), Fluence backlog 6.4bn (+30%) with 850M of data-center awards; Tesla's energy customer prepayments rose from 2.04bn to 3.30bn in nine months and its energy RPO is 10.73bn (10.42bn at end-2025). Paid driverless ride-hailing is a real market led by Waymo (about 500,000 paid rides a week earlier in 2026, 11 cities; press relay of Waymo statements). No attributed study sizing the robotaxi or humanoid-robot market was read.

bottleneck_potential.reading: Vehicles: Tesla is not a bottleneck. Listed installed capacity is at least 2.525 million a year (Model 3/Y 2.25 million, Cybertruck 125k, Cybercab 125k, Semi 25k) against Q3 2026 production of 464,391 (about 1.86 million annualized, about 74% of the listed floor; my arithmetic). Management says demand exceeds production, with the largest backlog in four years and battery availability as the limit (days of supply 11, versus 15 in Q2 and 27 in Q1): a management reading, while Q3 deliveries were still -2% year on year. Storage is the nearest thing to a bottleneck position: Tesla supplies deployable grid capacity at about 55 GWh a year (13.7 GWh in Q3) from 110 GWh of installed Megapack capacity (Texas 50 GWh began production in Q3); management calls Megapack 'almost sold out' for 2027 (call, opinion) and customer prepayments rose 62% in nine months. The binding input is cells: own LFP cells are 7 GWh in Nevada (early ramp, about 6% of Megapack capacity) and 4680 above 40 GWh, and the 10-K says Tesla relies on Panasonic and CATL with very few fully qualified suppliers. Competitors add capacity too (Fluence contract manufacturing, whose delays cut its fiscal-2026 revenue guide by about 0.4bn), so how long any scarcity lasts is not in the sources. Autonomy: the scarce thing is licensed unsupervised driving at scale; Tesla has the largest paid driver-assistance base (1.74 million active FSD subscriptions, +67% in a year) and nearly 2 million cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles, but Waymo holds the licensed paid driverless position today. SI training compute (225 MW installed, 400 MW guided by year end) is for internal use, not a sold scarce product. Optimus is a hypothesis only (early production, no paid customer, price or revenue).

share_trajectory.reading: Vehicles: flat-to-losing globally, gaining abroad. Tesla delivered 1,324,681 vehicles in January-September 2026, about 8.5% of Benchmark's 15.5 million plug-in and electric sales (the denominator includes plug-in hybrids; my arithmetic). Q3 deliveries fell 2% (486,532 vs 497,099) while the global market rose 3% year to date, so share was flat to lower; prior-year nine-month Tesla deliveries are not in the sources, so this is a direction, not a measured share series. BYD is the share-taker where Tesla also sells: overseas passenger and pickup sales of 1,342,960 in nine months (+92%), now equal to Tesla's whole global deliveries, while BYD's domestic units fell 33% (press relay of BYD data). Tesla also gains outside the US and China: Other international revenue +49.1% in nine months and Shanghai exports +58% in September (CPCA preliminary data, press). In the US the legacy makers are retreating from EVs (Ford Model e lost about 919M in Q2 2026 on about 1bn of revenue and discontinued the F-150 Lightning), while Rivian grows from a small base (19,248 deliveries in Q3, +46%, about 4% of Tesla's). Storage: Tesla deployments +9.6% in Q3 (13.7 vs 12.5 GWh) while Fluence's backlog grew 30% and its quarterly revenue 7.9%; no share percentage is computable (Tesla's figure is global, the market total US only). Robotaxi: Waymo leads in paid driverless rides; Tesla is not yet taking share on the numbers.

competitive_position.reading: Stronger than every named US EV maker on unit economics: Tesla's automotive gross margin excluding regulatory credits was 18.1% in Q3 2026 (16.3% in Q2; about 1.3 points of Q3 came from the 260M IEEPA tariff refund in automotive cost of sales, my arithmetic), against Ford Model e EBIT of about -919M on about 1bn of Q2 revenue and Rivian's Q2 2026 gross margin of 10.8% with an operating margin of -50%; GM's Q3 operating margin of 7.2% is company-wide (its EV margin was not verified). Revenue per non-lease delivery was flat (41,896 vs 41,816 a year earlier; the deck says ASP excluding FX was lower), so the lead rests on cost and scale, not price. Against BYD the comparison is open: BYD is larger in units (3.13 million in nine months, plug-in hybrids included) and growing abroad, but its H1 2026 revenue fell 7.1% and net profit 20.5% (net margin about 3.6%, my arithmetic); BYD's vehicle margins were not retrieved, so a cost lead either way is not evidenced. Storage: Tesla's energy gross margin was 33.1% in Q3 (about 23.8% after removing the net 187M of tariff refunds, before the unsized warranty true-down; my arithmetic) and 20.4% in Q2, against Fluence's 5.1% GAAP; Tesla's nine-month energy revenue of 8.43bn is about three times Fluence's fiscal-2026 guide of 2.9-3.1bn. Infrastructure: 84,465 Supercharger connectors (+14% in a year) and a record Services and other gross profit of 734M (15.9% margin). Autonomy: weaker than Waymo in licensed paid driverless operation (about 500,000 paid rides a week in 11 cities versus Tesla's nearly 2 million cumulative unsupervised miles), stronger in paid driver-assistance adoption (1.74 million FSD subscriptions; at least 75% of North American buyers sign up at delivery, with a free month).

threats.reading: (1) Chinese exporters, BYD first: BYD's overseas sales rose 92% in nine months to 1.34 million units, in the European and emerging markets that now carry Tesla's growth (Other international revenue +49.1% in nine months while United States -1.0% and China -1.4%). (2) Policy and regulation: US EV support is shrinking (North American EV sales -24% year to date; Tesla regulatory-credit revenue 417M to 113M and that RPO 841M to 384M); the 10-Q says tariffs and the One Big Beautiful Bill Act 'could significantly increase battery cell expenses', with the larger effect on energy storage, while own LFP cell capacity is only 7 GWh against 110 GWh of Megapack capacity; the Q3 tariff refunds (786M in cost of revenues less 339M owed to customers) are one-off. Autonomy needs approvals: the 10-K says EU and national rules may hinder autonomous vehicles and ride-hailing, and the 10-Q lists open NHTSA, SEC and DOJ information requests and the Benavides award (129M plus 200M punitive) on appeal. (3) Substitution in the US: the North American electric market fell 24% year to date and Tesla's US revenue fell 14.4% in Q3, while GM's Q3 operating income rose to 3.6bn from 1.1bn (its EV share of that not verified): a move back to combustion and hybrids is visible in market totals, not measured for Tesla's buyers. (4) A funded rival that already holds the scarce thing in autonomy: Waymo, inside Alphabet (34% operating margin and 44.9bn of capex in Q2 2026). (5) Supplier power in cells (Panasonic, CATL; very few qualified suppliers per the 10-K). (6) China: Shanghai holds about 38% of listed vehicle capacity and 18% of Megapack capacity, and China is 17.9% of nine-month revenue.

ההשקעות נשארות כ-20 מיליארד דולר בשנה בלי הכנסות מרובוטקסי ו-Optimus והרווח התפעולי נשאר נמוך: התזרים החופשי שלילי ב-2027-2028, והחברה מממנת את הפער מכ-21 מיליארד דולר מתוך כ-45 מיליארד המזומנים וההשקעות שלה, בלי למשוך מקווי האשראי.
מכסים וחוק OBBBA מייקרים את תאי הסוללה, בעיקר באנרגיה: הכנסות האנרגיה ירדו 16% ברבעון 3 והרווחיות הגבוהה שם נבעה מהחזרי מכס חד-פעמיים.
רגולציה ותביעות סביב נהיגה אוטונומית (בירורי NHTSA, פסק דין Benavides) מעכבות את הרחבת הרובוטקסי.
עסקה עם SpaceX (ועדה מיוחדת בוחנת אותה) בתנאים שמדללים את בעלי המניות.

growth_anchor.reason: No revenue guidance and the consensus is not citable yet, so the FY2027 step is built from Tesla's own record by line. Base +9%: car sales up mid-single digits as production rises (Q3 production 464k vs 408k in Q1, demand above production, days of supply 11, capacity 2.25M a year) but limited by batteries; services and other (+33% a year) and FSD up about 20%; energy up about 20% as the 50 GWh Houston Megafactory ramps (RPO 10.73bn); regulatory credits fall toward zero (RPO 384M). Nine-month 2026 growth was +12.5%, Q3 flat. Bear -3%: a repeat of FY2025 (-2.9%) as US (-14% in Q3) and China demand keep falling and exports meet BYD. Bull +20%: own cells lift the battery limit, Cybercab and Semi volume, Megapack near Houston capacity; close to the nine-month pace plus the new lines.

mature_margin.reason: GAAP operating margin after SBC. Own record FY2020-FY2025: 6.3%, 12.1%, 16.8%, 9.2%, 7.2%, 4.6% (median about 8.2%); Q3 2026 2.6% with R&D at 10% of revenue. Base 9%: the FY2023 level, reached as R&D intensity falls once Robotaxi, Optimus and Semi are commercialized (the CFO ties the opex rise to that) and services and energy (gross margin 16-20% and 20-30%) take a larger share. Bear 5%: the FY2025 level persists (price competition, no credits, AI spending stays). Bull 15%: near the FY2022 peak of 16.8%, with FSD software and a larger energy business lifting the mix.

sales_to_capital.reason: Revenue added per dollar of net investment (capex less depreciation, history.json). FY2021-FY2025: revenue +63.3bn on about 25.6bn net capex, about 2.5 (the plant ramp years: bull). FY2023-FY2025: revenue +13.4bn on about 16.3bn, about 0.8 (bear: capex into AI compute, cells and new lines that add little revenue). FY2026 capex of about 20bn against roughly 11bn of added revenue sits near the low end; base 1.5 assumes part of today's spending (cells, Megapack, Cybercab and Semi lines) starts to carry revenue.

maintenance_capex_pct.reason: Capex floor at management's guide (review repair). Guide: FY2026 capex 'approximately $20 billion' (call) / 'in excess of $20 billion' (10-Q); nine-month capex 13,014M, so Q4 2026 needs at least about 6.99B, prorated 65/92 to about 4.94B for the 2026-10-27..12-31 stub. The CFO said capex 'for the next few years would continue to expand' (Robotaxi fleet, Optimus capacity, solar, compute, a semiconductor fab); Musk: 'tens of billions' in 2028 (not quantified, so held at the 20B floor, not raised). Total capex (maintenance + growth at sales_to_capital) is held at about 4.94B in the stub and 20B in FY2027 and FY2028 in every scenario; the extra over the engine's maintenance rate (5.3% of revenue) sits on this line because it buys Robotaxi, Optimus, compute and the fab, which have no separate modelled revenue, so no revenue is credited for it. From FY2029 the engine rate returns (no company evidence for later years). Depreciation is not raised for the extra spend (no tax shield taken: conservative).

bear.reason_he: בתרחיש הדובי ההון החדש מרוויח רק כ־6% בשנה, כמו העסק כולו היום: ב־12 החודשים עד ספטמבר 2026 הרווח התפעולי היה 3.47 מיליארד דולר, כלומר כ־2.7 מיליארד אחרי מס (מס מונח 21%), על הון תפעולי של כ־54 מיליארד דולר (הון עצמי ועוד חוב, פחות 45 מיליארד מזומן והשקעות; מוניטין זניח נשאר בפנים) = כ־5%; ב־2025 כ־7%. מה נשבר: ההשקעות ב־2026 (13 מיליארד בתשעה חודשים, יותר מ־20 מיליארד בשנה, בעיקר מחשוב לבינה מלאכותית) והוצאות המחקר (עלו ב־69% ברבעון השלישי) לא מייצרות רווח נוסף; ברכבים המגבלה היא ביקוש ומחיר, ההכנסות מקרדיטים רגולטוריים נעלמות (113 מיליון ברבעון אחרי החזר של 475 מיליון), והרווחיות באנרגיה ברבעון השלישי כללה החזרי מכס חד־פעמיים. תשואה קרובה לצמיחה ארוכת הטווח (5%) ונמוכה ממחיר ההון נותנת מכפיל נמוך מאוד.

base.reason_he: בתרחיש הבסיסי ההון החדש מרוויח כ־12% בשנה. זה בערך הממוצע של טסלה בשנים 2023 עד 2025, אחרי שנת השיא: הרווח התפעולי אחרי מס (מס מונח 21%) היה 7.0, 5.6 ו־3.4 מיליארד דולר על הון תפעולי של כ־34, 36 ו־47 מיליארד (הון עצמי פחות מזומן והשקעות), כלומר כ־14% בממוצע (קצת פחות עם החוב, שלא נכלל ב־2023 ו־2024). זה פחות מ־15% של 2024 ויותר מ־5% עד 7% של היום, כי חלק גדול מההשקעה של 2026 עוד בבנייה ולא מרוויח, הרווחיות ברכבים בלי קרדיטים עלתה מ־16.3% ל־18.1%, והאנרגיה (רווח גולמי 3.8 מיליארד על 12.8 מיליארד הכנסות ב־2025, קיבולת של 110 GWh) מרוויחה יותר מהרכבים. הרובוטקסי והמחשוב לבינה מלאכותית עוד לא הוכיחו רווח, ולכן לא מניחים יותר. תשואה כזו, מעט מעל מחיר ההון, נותנת מכפיל בינוני ולא מכפיל של חברת צמיחה מוכחת.

bull.reason_he: בתרחיש השורי ההון החדש מרוויח כ־20% בשנה, כמו בפעם האחרונה שההשקעות של טסלה הצליחו: מ־2020 עד 2023, כשמפעלי שנגחאי, ברלין וטקסס התמלאו, הרווח התפעולי אחרי מס עלה בכ־5.4 מיליארד דולר על כ־31 מיליארד הון נוסף (כ־18%), ובשנת 2023 התשואה על ההון הייתה כ־21% עד 25%. לא לוקחים את שנות השיא 2021 עד 2022 (40% ומעלה), כי אלה היו מחירי רכב ורווחיות של שיא. כדי שזה יקרה, תוכנת הנהיגה העצמית צריכה להמשיך לגדול (1.7 מיליון מנויים לעומת 1.04 מיליון לפני שנה), הרובוטקסי ו־Cybercab (קיבולת 125 אלף בשנה) צריכים להפוך לשירות בתשלום רווחי, ו־Megapack צריך למלא את הקיבולת של 110 GWh (צבר הזמנות של 10.7 מיליארד דולר ומקדמות שעלו ל־3.3 מיליארד). הכלכלה של הרובוטקסי לא מדווחת, ולכן זה עוד לא הוכח.

own_history.years: 2021-2025 (16 quarter-end points 2021-12 to 2025-09: month-end price over the GAAP diluted EPS realised in the next four quarters, a hindsight proxy for the forward P/E)

key_risk.reading_he: המחיר נשען על רובוטקסי, FSD ו-Optimus שעדיין אין להן הכנסות מדווחות, בזמן שהכנסות הרכב לא צמחו: הכנסות רבעון 3 לא צמחו לעומת השנה שעברה, הרווח התפעולי רק 2.6% מההכנסות, וההוצאות על פיתוח והשקעות ממשיכות לעלות.

moat.note: Evidenced moat source: cost and scale in battery-electric vehicles and storage against named competitors (automotive gross margin ex credits 18.1% versus Ford Model e and Rivian losses; underlying energy margin about 24% versus Fluence 5.1%) plus the Supercharger network (84,465 connectors). Not evidenced against BYD (its margins were not retrieved). The advantage does not show in returns: operating margin fell from 16.8% (FY2022) to 4.6% (FY2025) and 2.6% in Q3 2026; the numbers lane's hand ROIC is about 7.3% for FY2025 and about 5.1% trailing (assumed 21% tax), below the 9.2% market cost of equity (risk-free 5.0% plus ERP 4.2%) before any company premium, and incremental ROIC is negative over the last nine months as capex doubled ahead of returns. Returns are already at or below the cost of capital; no mechanism in the company's numbers yet lifts them (autonomy and storage pricing would have to).

pricing_power.note: Vehicles: revenue per non-lease delivery flat at 41,896 versus 41,816 a year earlier even with a weaker dollar helping (the deck says ASP excluding FX was lower year over year, mix included). Storage: energy revenue -15.6% to 2,881M while deployments rose 9.6% (lower Megapack ASP, 339M of customer tariff refunds, fewer Powerwalls). Regulatory credits are shrinking. Management expects Megapack ASP to improve (opinion, not yet in the numbers). Services and other (+33%) is the one line with rising revenue.

retention.note: FSD churn, renewal and revenue per subscription are not disclosed. Active subscriptions rose from 1.04 to 1.74 million in a year and at least 75% of North American buyers sign up at delivery, but each delivery carries a free month, so that is a sign-up rate, not retention. Vehicle repurchase rates are not disclosed.

customer_concentration.note: Strong here means low concentration risk: consumer-driven, no customer at 10% or more of revenue. The related party SpaceX is 0.79% of Q3 revenue, but one unnamed customer exceeded 10% of receivables at 2026-09-30 and SpaceX owes 729M (about 16% of receivables), so the receivable, not the revenue, is concentrated.

market_size.note: Large and partly growing: 15.5 million plug-in and electric sales in nine months (+3%), record storage installations with data-center demand, and a paid robotaxi market proven by Waymo. Vehicle unit growth is flat, North America is shrinking, and the size of the robotaxi and humanoid markets is not quantified by any attributed study read.

competition.note: Weak here means the competitive environment is unfavourable to Tesla's prices: BYD's overseas units +92%, Tesla Q3 deliveries -2% with flat revenue per delivery; in storage Fluence's backlog +30%; in autonomy Waymo leads paid driverless rides. Tesla still gains against US EV makers and outside the US and China.

substitutes.note: Combustion and hybrid cars are winning back US buyers as incentives end (North America EV -24% year to date; Tesla US revenue -14.4% in Q3), but Europe's EV market is +30% and the global market +3%. In storage no substitute (gas peakers, other chemistries) was examined.

management.note: Delivered in 2026: Cybercab rides in Austin from 2026-09-03, Megapack Texas (50 GWh) and Semi volume production in Q3, FSD approved in nine EU countries, 30bn of committed credit lines. The only numeric guidance is capex and it moved: about 20bn (January), above 25bn (April, July), about 20bn (October), with 13.0bn spent in nine months. Most statements are timelines without numbers (Robotaxi 'noticeable probably in Q2' 2027, Optimus external deliveries late 2027, about 5 million vehicles a year by about 2030, EU-wide FSD by about Q1 2027): opinions to track, not evidence; no revenue guidance.

capital_allocation.note: Capex 13.0bn in nine months (about 20bn for 2026; management: 'tens of billions' by 2028 and Terafab 'north of 100bn' long term) against a hand ROIC of about 5-7% and negative incremental ROIC so far. No buybacks; shares outstanding rose from 3,751M to 3,953M in nine months (+5.4%, CEO award restricted shares); Q3 SBC 1,165M (663M a year earlier), with 9.74bn unrecognized for the 2025 CEO award's probable milestone and 105.8-120.4bn if the rest become probable. Related-party and non-core uses: 2.0bn in SpaceX stock (fair value 2.87bn), 962M of bitcoin, a 1.95bn hardware acquisition paid in stock. The balance sheet is strong (45.4bn cash and investments versus 9.5bn debt and finance leases). Weak on returns evidenced to date; that the front-loaded investment earns its cost is a hypothesis.

governance.note: The CEO also leads SpaceX (with xAI inside it, per the proxy) and the 10-K names key-person dependence. Related-party flows are growing: Megapack sales to SpaceX of 626M in nine months, a 729M receivable from SpaceX (588M billed for undelivered Megapacks) and 2.0bn invested in SpaceX stock. A board special committee is exploring a deeper SpaceX relationship 'including a business combination' (10-Q Item 5) and management declined questions on it. The 2025 CEO award holds 423.7M unearned restricted shares (about 10.7% of shares outstanding). The proxy says a management proposal to remove supermajority voting failed at the 2025 meeting.

regulation.note: Headwinds: regulatory-credit revenue 417M to 113M (after a 475M reversal) and its RPO 841M to 384M; US EV demand down 24% as support ends; tariffs and the One Big Beautiful Bill Act may raise cell costs, mostly for storage; Robotaxi and unsupervised FSD need state, federal and EU approvals, with NHTSA, SEC and DOJ information requests and product-liability cases open. In favour: FSD (Supervised) approved in nine EU countries. Unconfirmed press leads (an NHTSA petition on Robotaxi in school zones, a Cybercab certification order) were not used.

technology_ai.note: Paid adoption is real: 1.74 million active FSD subscriptions (+67% in a year) and automotive deferred revenue for FSD, connectivity and updates of 4.08bn (3.87bn at end-2025); unsupervised Robotaxi miles grew about eightfold in a quarter to nearly 2 million (management) and SI training compute is 225 MW (400 MW guided by year end). But FSD revenue is not disclosed, the 0.30 USD per paid mile Robotaxi goal is not reached, R&D runs at about 10% of revenue, and Waymo is ahead in licensed driverless operation. Not strong until paid unsupervised revenue shows in Tesla's own numbers.

geopolitics.note: China is 17.9% of nine-month revenue (22.1% in FY2025); Shanghai holds about 38% of listed vehicle capacity and 18% of Megapack capacity and now exports about half of its wholesale (CPCA preliminary, press); China working-capital debt is 5.97bn. Mitigants: local production in each main market and 82% of long-lived assets in the US. Cell imports and the tariff rate on them are not disclosed, so the Megapack tariff exposure is unsized.

cyclical.reason: Automotive is cyclical by industry, but Tesla's revenue history (2020-2025) shows a growth phase and a plateau, not a demand cycle, and the margin fall from 16.8% to 4.6% comes from price cuts, the end of regulatory credits and a deliberate AI/robotics R&D build. Normalizing to a mid-cycle margin would lift a trough that is structural; demand sensitivity to rates and incentives is carried in the bear case.
